newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Down slightly in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Down slightly in late trading.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps were slightly lower in late trading on Monday but sentiment remained strong on the back of a rally on gas oil futures on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE), brokers said.
IPE gas oil futures traded at $4.50 a tonne over its previous close at $218.25.
They said gas oil swaps players were also closely watching the well-offered physical market with early January offered at $32.30 a barrel.
Brokers said the rally in the west was on the back of colder weather expectations.
January gas oil paper was last traded at $31.65, and was last offered at $31.70, down from morning levsls of $31.95/$32.10. A number of traders were active as buyers, brokers said.
Naphtha firmed to $23.60/$24.00 per barrel, compared to $23.30/$23.40 on Friday.
But traders said naphtha was weakening with the crack for February Brent/first half February Tokyo open-spec down by around $2.00 since Friday to $64.00 per tonne.
Fuel oil's December swap was discussed at $120.50/$122.00 a tonne for January and $117.50/$119.00 for February.
